verdict.summary: Broadcom has the strongest current earnings power in the batch and one of the largest event risks. Fiscal Q2 2026 revenue rose 48% to $22.187 billion, GAAP net income was $9.31 billion and free cash flow $10.26 billion. AI semiconductor revenue reached $10.8 billion, up 143%, while infrastructure software contributed $7.18 billion and diversifies cash flow. Management guided Q3 revenue to approximately $29.4 billion, including $16.0 billion of AI semiconductor revenue, with 67% non-GAAP operating margin. The AI channel is both custom accelerators and networking silicon; VMware adds recurring software economics but also acquisition debt and integration concentration. At 43.4x EV/EBITDA and 24.2x EV/revenue, expectations are already extreme, while $64.91 billion debt remains material despite $19.63 billion cash. The 70/100 fundamental grade is defensible for growth, margin and free cash flow, not as a pre-earnings trade signal. Earnings are scheduled September 2, and no August 28 RTH opening bar was captured, so every displayed level remains inactive until a post-release review.

business.overview:
Broadcom combines semiconductor solutions with infrastructure software. Q2 FY2026 semiconductor revenue was $15.01B, or 68% of sales, while infrastructure software generated $7.18B, or 32%.

The AI channel runs through custom accelerators, switching, routing, connectivity and optical components supplied into hyperscale clusters. Q2 AI semiconductor revenue of $10.8B and Q3 expectation of $16.0B show direct monetization; VMware adds software cash flow from enterprise infrastructure rather than AI hardware units.

The model breaks if a hyperscale custom program changes vendor or schedule, networking content falls, or VMware integration and customer transitions erode software economics. Acquisition debt, customer concentration and export controls amplify those risks despite enormous free cash flow. Semiconductor and infrastructure-software cash flows have different drivers: AI accelerators and networking depend on hyperscaler capex, while VMware depends on subscription conversion and retention. The thesis breaks if AI concentration rises while VMware customer attrition, integration costs or debt service consume the expected cash conversion.
business.moat: Broadcom's moat is a portfolio of hard-to-replace connectivity franchises, deep custom-silicon co-development with hyperscalers and sticky mission-critical infrastructure software. Long qualification cycles and high switching costs support pricing, but custom-program concentration and VMware integration mean the moat is powerful rather than risk-free.

filingsReview.summary: 10 decision-relevant primary filing(s) are displayed with accession-specific findings. Grade B measures fundamentals; trade state wait measures timing and is evaluated separately.

filings.finding: The Q2 Form 10-Q reconciles 4.747B basic weighted-average shares to 4.876B diluted shares, a 129M incremental dilution effect. It also supports the $64.91B debt burden, VMware-influenced segment mix and semiconductor/customer concentration.
The July 6 Form 8-K supports the disclosed long-term Apple commercial agreement through 2031; it is an operating contract event and neither registers nor sells Broadcom common stock.

The June 17 Form 424B3 offers like-for-like exchanges of $750M 4.000% notes due 2029 and $1.2B 4.150% notes due 2032. Broadcom receives no proceeds and total debt does not increase; this is not equity financing.
The June 17 Form 424B3 covers exchanges of $3.249984B 3.137% notes due 2035 and $2.75B 3.187% notes due 2036. It produces no issuer proceeds or incremental debt and does not dilute common stock.
The January 6 Form 424B5 is the preliminary document for the four-series senior-note offering finalized on January 8; it is not counted as a separate financing.

The final January 8 Form 424B2 prices $4.5B of issuer senior notes: $750M 4.300% due 2031 and three $1.25B series at 4.600% due 2033, 4.950% due 2036 and 5.700% due 2056. This is debt with issuer proceeds, not common dilution.

The final September 24, 2025 Form 424B2 prices a separate $5.0B multi-series issuer senior-note offering. It is straight debt and must remain separate from the later no-proceeds exchange offers and from common-share dilution.

The FY2025 Form 10-K provides Broadcom’s audited semiconductor and infrastructure-software mix, VMware integration baseline, customer concentration, cash generation and debt obligations; it supports leverage analysis but records no 2026 common-stock issuance.

This June 17 EFFECT notice makes the related debt-exchange registration statement effective. It contains no sale amount, issuer proceeds, common shares or ATM authority and must not be counted as a separate financing transaction.

This second June 17 EFFECT notice concerns effectiveness of the companion debt-exchange registration. It does not issue securities, raise cash, increase debt or create common dilution independently of the mapped exchange prospectus.
